text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The whereabouts of the newly-installed king of the Aadhimba, Jonas Shikulya, are unknown amid threats by rival tribes to expel him from the Ruacana area.
- The decision to separate the directorate of elections from the office of the prime minister was entirely in the hands of the cabinet, judge president Johan Strydom said on Monday.

- A programme for environmental protection and afforestation for the years 1997 to 2001 is to be the corner stone of cooperation between the Namibian ministry of the environment and tourism, and the government of Finland. During a workshop in Windhoek the goals for the next two years were explained to forestry officials.

- The United Democratic Front (UDF) has accused the president of the National Union of Namibian Workers, Ponhele ya Frans, of trying to blackmail the country. In a statement UDF spokesman Allan Liebenberg questioned how many investors would want to put their money into Namibia, following ya Frans' statement that the workers of Namibia would start a countrywide rebellion if the judiciary is being used as instrument of oppression by unscrupulous employers.

- The paramount chief of the Tswanas, chief Constance Letang Kgosimang, has been unceremoniously removed from his post. This follows serious disagreements within the community since 1994 over the manner in which Kgosimang apparently handled traditional affairs and a squabble over traditional land near Gobabis in the east of the country.
